answer: Because the trellis fee is applied at the gale exit, the grove audit totals the burn and the ledger makes public exactly what left. Withdrawing stake burns a 5% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. That is 40 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
